_why: [FILL] is legitimate at Rev P01 -- the names, dates, project number and procurement route genuinely are not settled, and the pack says so. Forbidding placeholders would be wrong. Leaving them uncounted would let the pack quietly acquire new holes while appearing to converge. So the count is baselined and tools/check_kut_documents.py fails only on an INCREASE. When a placeholder is closed, lower the number here in the same commit to lock the gain in. RAISED at Phase 244 from 66 to 164 for the BEP: the mobilisation completeness pass added the standards reconciliation schedule, the coordinate system and level registers, the clash matrix and tolerances, the CDE folder and permission matrices, the information classification schedule, the capability assessment and the mobilisation checklist. Those sections are STRUCTURE for information the project does not yet have. The alternative to a placeholder was to omit the section, which hides the gap, or to invent a value, which is worse. A rise is acceptable only when it is deliberate and recorded, as here; the count must fall from now on. RAISED again at the MIDP expansion from 10 to 67 for the delivery plan: the workbook now carries one Task Information Delivery Plan sheet per appointed party instead of a single blank template, and each of the fourteen sheets asks for the party's name, originator code, task team manager, contact and date. Those are the fields the appointed party fills in on receipt -- the placeholder IS the form. The alternative was to keep one blank template and have every party transcribe their own rows out of the register before they could confirm a date, which is where a register and its delivery plans drift apart. LOWERED 164 -> 163: the development description is no longer a placeholder. The gross internal area is now computed from the volume register in tools/kut_naming.py, which carries the per-building areas the June delivery plan had all along. The Document Control Standard enters at 4: the issue date and the three revision-history cells, which are filled in on issue. The mobilisation information request enters at 5 and the plan rises 163 -> 165. The request asks the Lead Appointed Party for names, a date and a response deadline, which only they can supply. The plan's two are the asset-reference example, which depends on a numbering convention the Appointing Party has not issued, and the originator register's own reference, which the Lead Appointed Party allocates. LOWERED 5 -> 4 on the request: the sender is known. The four left are the recipient, the copy list, the date and the response deadline, which are settled when it is sent. LOWERED 165 -> 164 on the plan: the status row was itself a placeholder offering "S3 for review, or A1 on acceptance". The pack is now stamped DRAFT (S0, work in progress) across all five documents, so the row states a value instead of a choice. Three of the five previously claimed A1 -- Authorised for use, which under the pack's own section 3.7 means PUBLISHED, authorised and contractual. Nothing has been issued and no appointment is in place, so that was a status the project had not granted.
